newsitem.title: FRANCE: French navy ship explodes off Cherbourg, two dead.
newsitem.headline: French navy ship explodes off Cherbourg, two dead.

text.p: Two people were killed and three were missing after a French navy ship carrying ordnance experts blew up and sank off the Channel port of Cherbourg on Wednesday, the navy said.

A rescue service official said at least four other people were seriously wounded and flown by helicopter to a military hospital after the explosion aboard the 450-tonne support ship La Fidele off Cape Levy.
He said two explosions had been heard up to 30 km (19 miles) away.
A navy spokesman said there were 16 crew and six civilian ordnance experts aboard the 54-m (160-ft) vessel.
The men had been on their way to a live-firing exercise at sea and the blast at about 10.30 a.m. (0830 GMT) was apparently caused by the explosives aboard, the spokesman said.
Five rescue ships and a helicopter were despatched to the scene. An investigation was launched into the cause of the accident.
